thread:
lara: Heads-up — noticed p99 token latency increase on streaming chat routes after yesterday's canary. p95 jumped from ~30ms to ~120ms for a subset of requests.

adrian: Which exact route and model variant? hosted or dedicated?

lara: Only /v1/chat/stream so far. Happens on dedicated Ampere pools and occasionally on hosted. Metric panels show spike starting at 12:10 UTC. Link: https://grafana/redwood/d/streams (internal)

mike: I pulled a short perf profile on an affected canary. Kernel selector appears to pick the int8 matmul path for small seq lengths after the quant selector tweak. For seqs <= 16, the int8 kernel is slower here (cache behavior + kernel launch overhead). Quick excerpt from profiler:

```text
[profile] seq=16 kernel=matmul_int8 time_us=85
[profile] seq=8 kernel=fp16_mm time_us=40
[profile] kv_hit=true kv_latency_us=5
```

mike: Also noticed the streaming chunk cadence has larger inter-chunk gaps server-side — p99 stream_chunk_gap_ms spiked to ~350ms.

sami: FYI we rolled batching window from 20ms -> 40ms in the canary to improve throughput. That change can increase per-token tail latency when request concurrency is low (fewer coalesced ops). Might explain part of the regression.

perf-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT stream_chunk_gap_ms.p99 > 300ms for route=chat/stream (since 2026-03-18T12:12:00Z). See alert runbook: /runbooks/streaming-chunk-gap

adrian: We need better token-level breakdowns on the dashboard: separate metrics for
- kernel_exec_ms (per-token)
- batching_wait_ms (time waiting for batch window)
- kv_lookup_ms (per-token)
- network_send_ms (server->client chunk send)
Add client_vs_server_delta measurement: client_first_chunk_arrival_ts - server_first_chunk_send_ts. Right now client-observed stalls look worse than server metrics indicate.

lara: Also saw spikes in kv invalidation logs around the same time — maybe TTL or shard tuning changed during canary. Current kv config on canary:

```yaml
kv_cache:
  ttl_ms: 60000
  shard_size: 1024
```

mike: Actionable plan:
1) Revert the quant selector tweak for the canary (fast revert to previous kernel heuristics). I'll open the revert PR and mark it high priority.
2) Reduce batching window to 20ms on the canary and run A/B for 1 hour.
3) Add server-side metric server_chunk_gap_ms and a client delta metric (adrian's suggestion) to Grafana; surface route-level p95/p99 token latency.
4) Add a synthetic streaming probe (low-QPS) that exercises short sequences to catch regressing kernels early.

lara: I'll open the dashboard/alert PR with the new panels and synthetic probe config. Assigning kernel revert to @mike. Thanks everyone — tagging oncall in case alert escalates. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-317. Auto-assigned to eng-runtime oncall.
